prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-25, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-25):
| Current ratio           | 0.42 |
| Retained earnings       | 261,693M |
| Current liabilities     | 2,559,605M |
| Current assets          | 1,067,083M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 303,243M |
| Total liabilities       | 3,107,151M |
| Total assets            | 3,410,394M |
| EBIT / operating income | 12,435M |
| Revenue                 | 49,691M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows very weak liquidity (current ratio 0.42) and extremely high leverage (debt to assets ~0.91, debt much larger than equity), despite a solid EBIT margin. These factors imply material credit risk and a non-investment-grade rating, likely in the lower speculative range.

DECISION: BB-
